title: Binary x data scaling: does the 108-bit Hamming code inherit the frozen family's steep Q(n), and does data buy back M114's 3.3-point bit loss?

device._note: sign-code projection on CPU numpy (float64); the Hamming GEMM (sign-GEMM identity, bit-identical to the CPU hardware-POPCNT path) on the GPU; ridge on CPU. HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1, gfx1201.

parity_guard.feature: CLS token concatenated with the mean of the patch tokens

sparse.random_dictionary: M108/M113/M114 exact: prefix of the seeded permutation of the shared 8192-whitened-patch pool (seed 11)
sparse.hash_learned: ITQ (Gong et al., CVPR 2011) with M114's exact registered parameters; hash_control = seeded Gaussian projection
sparse.hamming: sign-GEMM identity (bit-identical to packed uint64 XOR + POPCNT); triangle kernel on Hamming, soft assignment over ALL atoms

scaling.subsample_rule: first n rows of the M107-shuffled train order (nested), identical to M116
scaling.test_set: the full 34500-row shared test set, identical for every ladder point and both arms
scaling.float_reference_curve: M116 sealed sparse Q(n): 0.0484/0.0706/0.0952/0.1442/0.1935/0.2153 (gain 0.1668); binary codes are image functions, so each arm's codes are encoded ONCE into D: memmaps and a ridge is fitted at each n

gate.t1_reference: M114 sealed b_random (RANDOM-108) = 0.1842 at n=138000, reproduced within 0.002
gate.kill_switch_1_binary_steepness: fired if the binary arm's Q(n) gain across the ladder is < 0.5 x the float arm's gain (0.1668): the 108-bit code must inherit at least half of the frozen family's data-scaling steepness
gate.kill_switch_2_bit_loss_buyback: fired if the binary-vs-float gap at n_max exceeds the gap at n_min + 0.01: data must NARROW (or hold) the M114 bit loss, else data does not buy back the 3.3-point loss and M114's KS2 failure is not rescued at scale
gate.registered_prediction: the binary code is a lossy projection of the same 12288-wide feature; if its Q(n) is comparably steep (same wide head), the gap should narrow as data grows - the M114 rescue test
